title: Pokemon Pokopia Block Float Recipe & Unlock Guide
description: Craft Block Floats in Pokemon Pokopia: unlock the 500-Coin recipe at Bubbly Basin Environment Level 2, use Stardust Rock and Pokémetal, then build underwater.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokemon Pokopia Block Float Recipe & Unlock Gameplay Guides 2026-08-07 Pokemon Pokopia Block Float Recipe & Unlock Craft Block Floats in Pokemon Pokopia: unlock the 500-Coin recipe at Bubbly Basin Environment Level 2, use Stardust Rock and Pokémetal, then build underwater. Author : Pokopia Guide Team The Block Float is the practical building block for structures that do not touch the seafloor. It can support objects and buildings on water or underwater, making it much easier to create suspended rooms, platforms, and underwater houses without first constructing a pillar from the ground. Block Float Recipe and Unlock Requirement Detail Recipe source Bubbly Basin shop Shop unlock Bubbly Basin Environment Level 2 Recipe price 500 Coins Crafting material Stardust Rock ×1 Crafting material Pokémetal ×1 Raise Bubbly Basin to Environment Level 2 before looking for the recipe. The shop will then sell it for 500 Coins. Craft each Block Float with one Stardust Rock and one Pokémetal . What a Block Float Does Use a Block Float as a temporary or permanent foothold in water. It is useful whenever the structure you want to place has no contact with the ground. The item description specifically identifies it as a float for building on or under water and for making objects float. The important rule is that blocks placed on top of a Block Float remain in place after the Block Float is removed . You do not need to leave a large number of floats inside the finished build. A few floats are enough to establish the first layer; remove or relocate them once the rest of the structure is placed. How to Build Underwater with Block Floats Learn Dive and bring the Block Floats to the desired depth. Place one at the height where you want to start the structure. Place normal blocks or objects on and around the float to make the first platform. Extend the platform and build walls, floors, or a house as usual. Remove the temporary float when the placed blocks are stable, then reuse it for another section. This method is most helpful when building far above the seafloor. A ground-to-platform pillar still works, but it takes more blocks and is slower to remove afterward. Plan the First Layer Before You Place It The first layer is the part of a suspended build that determines everything above it. Decide the floor height and footprint before spending materials on walls or decoration. For a small room, place one float near the center, make a compact floor around it, then expand outward. For a wider platform, establish several points across the planned footprint before joining them with regular blocks. This avoids discovering too late that one edge sits at the wrong height. Keep the floats accessible while working. A float that is completely enclosed by walls, furniture, or a finished floor is harder to recover. Treat it as temporary scaffolding: build the usable first layer, remove the float, then finish the visual details. This is also useful when testing an underwater design, since you can reposition the same material rather than committing to a permanent support layout. Where Block Floats Work Best Block Floats are not only for a full underwater house. They are practical for a small observation deck above the bottom, a bridge-like route between raised sections, a furniture display set at water level, or a room that you want to look suspended inside a larger underwater build. They work best when the desired starting point has no natural surface nearby. For simple ground-level decoration, building directly on the seafloor is usually quicker. Save Block Floats for designs where their ability to start in open water removes a real constraint. Carry several on a long Dive trip, but do not overcraft them: the same float can be collected and moved after each first layer is complete. Block Floats vs. Construction Kits Construction Kits can be placed without first making a block foothold. Use them when the building itself has a kit and you only need to place the finished structure. Use Block Floats when you are designing a custom build block by block, placing furniture at a chosen height, or making an underwater platform before adding details. Situation Better choice Place a premade building kit Construction Kit Build a custom underwater room Block Float Add a floating furniture platform Block Float Reach a very high underwater point Block Float Common Mistakes Looking for the recipe before Environment Level 2 The recipe is not in the initial Bubbly Basin shop inventory. Raise Environment Level first, then return with 500 Coins. Treating every Block Float as permanent support Blocks placed on top stay after the float is destroyed. Recover the float after setting the structure's first layer instead of crafting one for every tile. Building from the seafloor by default Pillars from the ground remain a valid method, but Block Floats are faster when the target is high above the bottom or when you want a clean suspended design. Forgetting to bring materials before a long Dive The recipe is cheap per float, but the useful building materials are the blocks and furnishings placed afterward. Bring the planned floor blocks, a few spare floats, and any furniture before heading deep into Bubbly Basin. Returning to restock is possible, but it interrupts a build more than preparing the first layer on shore. title: Pokopia Multiplayer Guide: Co-op & Modes Guide
description: Multiplayer guide for Pokemon Pokopia. Host and join, Palette Town vs Cloud Island vs Guest Mode, couch co-op, unlock at Env. Level 2, host vs guest item rules.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokopia Multiplayer Guide: Co-op & Modes Gameplay Guides 2026-03-19 Pokopia Multiplayer Guide: Co-op & Modes Multiplayer guide for Pokemon Pokopia. Host and join, Palette Town vs Cloud Island vs Guest Mode, couch co-op, unlock at Env. Level 2, host vs guest item rules. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Find multiplayer partners on Discord Use the community server for co-op partners, trades, and multiplayer help. Join our Discord How to Play Multiplayer Playing as a Host Select " Play via Communications " from the PC in the Pokémon Center. Select " Invite others to your town ". Choose either Internet Communication or Local Communication (Internet requires a Nintendo Switch Online membership). Configure the multiplayer settings and press the + Button to confirm. When playing in towns other than Palette Town, it will be in Visit Mode only, and moves or items cannot be used. Shared Play is for Palette Town only Multiplayer using Shared Play can only be done in Palette Town . If you want to play in "Palette Town" The host should move through the map to Palette Town. The guest does not need to move there themselves. When the host moves to a different town, a confirmation prompt will appear for the guest. Playing as a Guest Select " Play via Communication " from the PC in the Pokémon Center Select " Visit a friend's town " For Internet communication, enter the Link Code (shared by the host) Confirm the destination and select it Types of Multiplayer Features of Each Multiplayer Mode Type Features Palette Town Can build together, shared play supported, guests cannot take items back Cloud Island Can build even when the host is away, viewing only is also possible in Virtual Mode, items cannot be taken back (Host can only learn recipes) Guest Mode (Story Towns) Viewing only, set in towns visited during the story Recommendations by Playstyle Purpose Recommendation Build together (Shared Play) Palette Town Build together (Host offline OK) Cloud Island Show your story town Guest Mode Explore Cloud Island freely Virtual Mode What You Can Do in Multiplayer Build on Cloud Island Cloud Island is a multiplayer island where you can progress with town building even when the host is away. Up to 4 players can play simultaneously, and since there is no limit on players swapping in and out, many players can participate. You cannot take Pokémon or items back with you (applies to both hosts and guests). Building in Palette Town Palette Town is a place where you can enjoy building your town freely. Up to 4 players can play together at once, and all participants can contribute to town-building by placing blocks and more. Only the host can take back Pokemon and items. Guests cannot. View Towns in Spectator Mode Multiplayer in towns other than Fresh Town will be in Spectator Mode. Guests cannot use moves or items. Invite Pokemon to Your Town If you talk to a Pokemon in the host's town twice, you can select "Come visit my place next time." If you give a "Star Piece" to a visiting Pokemon, you will receive a "Souvenir." Opening the souvenir in an empty habitat will make a Pokemon of the same species appear. Take Commemorative Photos During multiplayer, you can enjoy taking commemorative photos with other players using the in-game camera function. You can also take selfies using the in-camera mode. Multiplayer Unlock Conditions It is unlocked by raising the Environment Level of the Withered Wastelands to 2 . This can be reached in about 1 hour from the start of the game. Differences Between Host and Guest Item Host Guest Bring back Pokemon ○ (Fresh Town only) ✕ Bring back items ○ (Fresh Town only) ✕ Bring back from Cloud Island ✕ (Recipe acquisition only) ✕ Management functions (Town travel/Settings) ○ ✕ On Cloud Island, neither the host nor the guest can bring back Pokemon or items. title: Pokemon Pokopia Smoothies: Mixer Unlock, All Recipes, and Underwater Surf Guide
description: Make Smoothies in Pokemon Pokopia with Cut Watermelon and two ingredients. Unlock the Mixer through Mudkip's Bubbly Basin request, use Surf while Diving, and check all six known Smoothie recipes and offering effects.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokemon Pokopia Smoothies: Mixer Unlock, All Recipes, and Underwater Surf Gameplay Guides 2026-08-07 Pokemon Pokopia Smoothies: Mixer Unlock, All Recipes, and Underwater Surf Make Smoothies in Pokemon Pokopia with Cut Watermelon and two ingredients. Unlock the Mixer through Mudkip's Bubbly Basin request, use Surf while Diving, and check all six known Smoothie recipes and offering effects. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Smoothies are the key food for faster underwater travel in Bubbly Basin. Drink one to use Surf while Diving : Ditto turns into Lapras and can move through the sea more quickly. Every known recipe begins with Cut Watermelon , so prepare Watermelon Seeds and a Pokemon with the Cut Trees specialty before you unlock the Mixer. Unlock the Mixer The Mixer is a reward from a Mudkip request that appears after completing the Bubbly Basin story. Once it is available, put Cut Watermelon and two other ingredients into the Mixer to make a Smoothie. Whole Watermelon does not substitute for Cut Watermelon. Give Watermelon to a Pokemon with the Cut Trees specialty first. See Watermelon and Cut Watermelon: Locations and Uses for the seed unlock and processing route. Why Smoothies Matter Drinking any Smoothie upgrades Surf during Dive. It is valuable when you are repeatedly crossing Bubbly Basin, entering long caves, or collecting materials around the underwater town. While boosted Surf is active, you can dash underwater and use Whirlpool to break blocks by holding ZR. Prepare a Smoothie before leaving a convenient Mixer instead of waiting until you are already deep underwater. Known Smoothie Recipes Smoothie Ingredients Offering effect Watermelon Smoothie Cut Watermelon + two ingredients that do not make another dish Ancient items appear somewhat more often Sea Grapes Smoothie Cut Watermelon + Sea Grapes + one ingredient Ho-Oh and Lugia appear somewhat more often Leppa Smoothie Cut Watermelon + Leppa Berry + one ingredient Ancient items appear somewhat more often Red Hot Smoothie Cut Watermelon + Ripe Carrot + one ingredient; requires a Burn-specialty Pokemon Pokemon appear in habitats somewhat more often Refreshing Soda Smoothie Cut Watermelon + Soda Pop + Aspear Berry Better shop stock appears much more often Coffee Parfait Smoothie Cut Watermelon + Moomoo Milk Coffee + any bread Rare items are found much more often The last column applies when the Smoothie is offered. Recipe ingredients should be checked before mixing: a flexible slot can accept an ingredient that does not turn the result into a different dish. Cut Watermelon Is the Ingredient to Stockpile The main bottleneck is usually not the Mixer itself but maintaining enough Cut Watermelon. Watermelon has to be grown and then processed by a Pokemon with the Cut Trees specialty before it becomes usable in a Smoothie. Keep a small reserve after harvesting rather than immediately using every piece, especially once you start planning longer Dive routes. The other two slots determine which named Smoothie you make. A basic Watermelon Smoothie is the economical option when you only need underwater Surf, because it can use flexible ingredients such as Leaves. Named recipes are worth saving for a specific offering target. This keeps valuable ingredients from being used just for movement when a cheaper Smoothie would give the same Dive and Surf access. Drinking a Smoothie and Offering One Are Different Decisions Drink a Smoothie when the immediate goal is underwater travel. Its direct benefit is Surf while Diving, which helps with a long cave, repeated travel through Bubbly Basin, or a material route that would otherwise take several slow trips. Offer a Smoothie when you want the recipe's listed secondary effect. For example, Sea Grapes Smoothie is the relevant choice when pursuing Ho-Oh or Lugia, while Refreshing Soda is the one to reserve for better shop stock. The movement benefit is shared by all Smoothies, so the special ingredients only need to be spent when the offering effect is part of your plan. Before You Start a Deep Route Check four things before leaving the town: you have learned Dive, you have Cut Watermelon rather than whole Watermelon, you have made the Smoothie you intend to drink, and you have not accidentally spent a rare named-recipe ingredient meant for an offering. That short check avoids the common problem of reaching a distant cave entrance with a whole Watermelon or an empty Mixer inventory. Efficient Smoothie Preparation Reach Bubbly Basin Environment Level 2 and buy Watermelon Seeds. Grow Watermelon, then ask a Cut Trees-specialty Pokemon to make Cut Watermelon. Finish the Bubbly Basin story and Mudkip's request to obtain the Mixer. Make several Smoothies before a long Dive route. Keep special ingredients such as Sea Grapes, Leppa Berries, Psy Soda, and Moomoo Milk for the offering effects you want. Choosing a Recipe Make a basic Watermelon Smoothie when the only goal is underwater Surf and you do not want to spend rare ingredients. Choose Sea Grapes Smoothie when looking for Ho-Oh or Lugia, and use the other named recipes when their offering bonus matches your current goal. The Mixer is also a reason not to process just one Watermelon at a time: a small reserve of Cut Watermelon lets you react to the ingredient you find. Smoothie FAQ Can I Surf while Diving without a Smoothie? No. The Smoothie is the confirmed item that enables Surf during Dive. Why does the Mixer reject my Watermelon? The recipe needs Cut Watermelon . Process the whole fruit through a Pokemon with the Cut Trees specialty. Do all Smoothies improve underwater movement? Yes. The named recipes all upgrade Surf while Diving; their ingredient differences determine the offering effect. title: Pokopia Bleak Beach Town Walkthrough Guide
description: Walkthrough for Bleak Beach Town in Pokemon Pokopia. Learn Magnet Rise, rescue Vaporeon, encounter Spiritomb, trigger sandstorms, unlock doors, and meet Suicune.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokopia Bleak Beach Town Walkthrough Story Walkthrough 2026-03-18 Pokopia Bleak Beach Town Walkthrough Walkthrough for Bleak Beach Town in Pokemon Pokopia. Learn Magnet Rise, rescue Vaporeon, encounter Spiritomb, trigger sandstorms, unlock doors, and meet Suicune. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Bleak Beach Town Walkthrough Go through the gate to the east of Withered Wastelands Town Head to Gloomy Beach Town from the Area Gate on the east side of Withered Wastelands Town. Please note that you must clear Withered Wastelands Town and reach Super Trainer Rank to pass through the gate. Event occurs at the broken bridge further along the path Once you arrive at Bleak Beach Town, follow the path. A conversation with Tangrowth will begin at the broken bridge further ahead. Connect the Broken Bridge by Placing Blocks Place blocks between the gaps of the broken bridge to connect it. Any type of block can be used, but you can use the "Seaside Sand" found near the bridge even if you don't have any blocks in your inventory. Event at the Pokemon Center on the Left After Crossing the Bridge An event will occur at the broken Pokemon Center located on the left after crossing the bridge. The event will progress after you talk to Tangrowth and then check the PC. Place Blocks to Stop the Water Flow To stop the water flowing toward the Poke Center, go up to the upper area and place a block. By placing a block in the water flow located directly above the Poke Center, you can dam the water. Talk to Meowth and Follow Him After talking to Tangrowth, speak to the Meowth standing nearby. Once the conversation ends, Meowth will start moving, so follow him to proceed. Damming the water behind Meowth's house Go behind Meowth's house, destroy the wood debris with Cut, and then place a block to dam the water. By stopping the water, the "Resting Place" habitat will be restored. Create New Habitats and Discover 2 Pokémon ▲ Recommended habitats that are easy to create Check the Habitat Dex in the menu, create new habitats, and discover 2 undiscovered Pokémon. Finding them will allow the story to progress. Talk to Meowth and Accept the Request When you talk to Meowth, you will be asked to bring two "Mushroom Lamps." Mushroom Lamps can be crafted using the Glowing Mushrooms found in caves. Head to the Cave and Obtain Glowing Mushrooms The Glowing Mushrooms used for the Mushroom Lamp are located inside the cave. By heading back to the bridge you first visited and proceeding northeast, you can spot the Glowing Mushrooms even from a distance. Place the Mushroom Lamp in Meowth's Room Once you have crafted two Glowing Mushrooms into a Mushroom Lamp, place it in Meowth's Room. Any location within the room is fine. Talk to Meowth again and accept the request Meowth is having trouble cleaning up the mud in front of the house. Talk to Meowth and accept the request. Create a Habitat and Befriend Piplup To befriend Piplup, let's create the "Lush Yellow Grass" habitat. The Lush Yellow Grass habitat can be created by placing four grass patches near the water. Take Piplup to the mud and wash it away to clear Once you become friends with Piplup, take it to the mud in front of Meowth's house. After Piplup puts bubbles on the mud, wash the mud away with Water Gun to complete the request. Receive a Request from Tangrowth When you talk to Tangrowth and accept the request, you will be told to build a house and prepare three pieces of furniture. Purchase a "Sand Room Kit" from the shop and build a house in a location of your choice. Gather Materials and Pokémon to Build a House You can start construction by gathering materials and bringing two Pokémon. Once completed, put up a "Ditto Flag" and place three pieces of furniture. Makuhita is Recommended for the Construction Pokémon Slot For the construction Pokémon slot, Makuhita is recommended as its habitat is easy to create. Grow four patches of grass on a large tree to create the "Yellow Grass in the Shade" habitat. Report to Tangrowth to Complete the Request Once you have built a house and placed 3 pieces of furniture, report to Tangrowth to complete the request. Receive a Request from Meowth Go to Meowth's home and talk to it. You will be asked to place a planter made of bricks. Create a Habitat and Become Friends with Torchic Create a habitat for Torchic and become friends with it in order to make bricks. The materials needed for the habitat are available in front of Meowth's home. Have Torchic Make Bricks Directly behind Torchic's habitat, you can find "Squishy Clay," the material used for bricks. After breaking the blocks to obtain it, give it to Torchic to have it processed. Craft a Planter Once you receive the Bricks from Torchic, let's craft a Planter at the Crafting Table. Place Near Meowth's Habitat Let's place the planter you made near Meowth's habitat. Planting Flowers in Planters Flowers are blooming right next to Meowth's home, so collect them using the move "Cultivate" and plant them in the planter you've set up. You can pick up flowers with ZR using Cultivate, then move to the planter and press A to plant them. Receive a Request from Piplup Accept a request from Piplup, who is with Professor Tangrowth. You will be asked to build a shower. Create a Habitat and Befriend Trubbish To befriend Trubbish, pick up 3 pieces of "Non-burnable Trash" scattered across the field. Use one as a material to craft a "Trash Bag," and keep the other two to give to Trubbish. By placing them near the trash can next to the Pokémon Center, you can create the "Trash Collection Point" habitat. Give the Non-burnable Trash to Trubbish Give the remaining "Non-burnable Trash" to Trubbish and have it take out the "Iron." Craft a Shower and Place it in Piplup's Habitat Craft a Shower using the "Iron" you received from Trubbish. You'll be told to place it in "a good spot," but placing it near Piplup's habitat is fine. Showers Must be Attached to a Wall Showers can only be placed on walls. If there is no wall where you want to install it, you can place a single block to make it possible to install. Report to Piplup After installing the shower, talk to Piplup to clear the request. Receiving a Request from Tangrowth Let's accept a request from Tangrowth, who is located in front of the Pokémon Center. You will be required to reach Environment Level 3, but this can be achieved by completing all subsequent requests. Receiving a Request from Trubbish Let's also listen to the request from the Trubbish located near Tangrowth. You will be asked to light up the streetlights, which involves bringing a Pawmi that can use "Generate Electricity." Create a Habitat and Befriend Pawmi On the small island to the left when facing the Pokémon Center, you can find the flowers needed for Pawmi's habitat. Use the move "Cultivate" to gather four of them in one spot to create the habitat. Clear by bringing Pawmi to the front of the Pokemon Center Take Pawmi to the front of the Pokemon Center and have them turn on the streetlights. Trubbish's request will be cleared, so next, talk to Pawmi and listen to their request. Stop the water leak near the center of the map To complete Pawmi's request, you will need Mareep. Since Mareep's habitat is submerged in the flooded area at the center of the map, let's stop the water leak with blocks to restore the habitat. Talk to the Mareep that appeared from the habitat Become friends with the Mareep that appeared from the habitat, then talk to it again to receive "Cotton". Report to Pawmi to Complete Give Pawmi the "Wool" you received from Mareep to complete Pawmi's request. Receiving a Request from Piplup When you talk to Piplup, you will receive a request to go swimming together. Create a Habitat and Befriend Lapras Befriend Lapras so you can swim together with Piplup. Lapras's habitat can be created at the seaside using four hedges and a large tree. Obtain Healthy Hedge Seeds near the Pokémon Center The "hedges" required for Lapras's habitat can be created by growing "Healthy Hedge Seeds" found near the Pokémon Center. They are located inside a Poké Ball within a broken house at the end of the path behind the Pokémon Center. Wash away the mud on the map for Lapras's request After becoming friends with Lapras, you will be asked to wash away 80 patches of mud on the map. Let's clean them up by cooperating with Piplup, just like before. Learn "Surf" from Lapras Once you complete Lapras's request, you will be able to transform into Lapras and use "Surf." By pressing the R button while in the water, you can transform into Lapras and move across the water as long as your PP lasts. Talk to Piplup and Swim in the Sea Together to Clear After talking to Piplup and moving to the coast, you can clear the request by using "Surf" to swim in the sea together. Note that Piplup will not swim unless you talk to it while transformed into Lapras. Raise the Environment Level to 3 You cannot proceed to the next chart, "Let's Brighten Up the Town!", unless you have reached Environment Level 3. If you have completed the Pokemon requests up to this point, it should rise naturally. If it's not enough, it's efficient to pick up the sparkles on the island to create new habitats and increase the number of undiscovered Pokemon. How to Raise Environment Level and Unlocked Elements Habitat Pokedex List Receive a Request from Trubbish Talk to Trubbish to receive a request. After checking Environment Level 3 on the PC and talking to Tangrowth, Trubbish will run to the vicinity of the Pokemon Center. Go to the place where the sound is coming from and break the wall Go to the place where the sound is coming from and break the wall with Rock Smash. Examine Snorlax inside the cave Enter the cave and examine Snorlax. Guide Tangrowth to Snorlax's Location Talk to Tangrowth and head to the location where Snorlax is together. Since Tangrowth has a large body and cannot enter the cave unless the entrance is widened, you will need to widen the entrance slightly. "Let's Brighten Up the Town!" Triggered As the conversation progresses, the Important Request "Let's Brighten Up the Town" will be triggered. In order to wake up Snorlax, let's cooperate with Pokémon and brighten up the town. Receive a Request from Meowth Talk to Meowth to accept a request. Light up the streetlights with Pawmi Travel with a "Power Generation" Pokemon like Pawmi or Mareep and go around lighting up the streetlights. You will be able to clear the Request once you light 3 of them, but it's better to light up more to help with the story progression later on. Report to Meowth to Complete After lighting the streetlights, talk to Meowth to complete the request. Talk to Torchic Talk to Torchic to accept its request. Since you need to report back after lighting the fire, it is recommended to have Torchic accompany you while the request is in progress. Creating the "Preparing a Meal at the Resort" Habitat Let's create the "Preparing a Meal at the Resort" habitat. All necessary materials can be made through crafting, and the large palm tree is located on the Pokemon Center side. Report to Torchic to Complete Once you have created the habitat, report to Torchic to complete the request. Talk to Tangrowth inside the cave Tangrowth inside the cave has a speech bubble, so let's go and talk to it. Head to the Scene of the Commotion After the conversation event with Tangrowth, head towards the commotion in town. Examining the fallen Pokemon will trigger a conversation event. Talk to Usu-chu You can talk to Usu-chu and become friends during the conversation. Take Usu-chu to Snorlax's Location Talk to Usu-chu again, select "Let's go together," and take them to where Snorlax is. Usu-chu walks at a slow pace and takes a while to arrive, so it is efficient to bring Piplup or Pawmi along and maintain the town as you go. Place a Shell Lamp near Snorlax After the event in the cave, craft a Shell Lamp and place it near Snorlax. Lighting it up with Pawmi or Mareep will complete Usuchu's request. Follow Usu-chu Follow Usu-chu as they walk toward the town. You will be guided to the Windmill Power Machine, and you can accept a request by talking to them. Connecting the Wind Power Generator and Power Poles Take one of the power poles near the wind power generator and place it. As a guide for the placement range, if a connection can be made while holding a power pole, it will be displayed as semi-transparent. Talk to Usu-chu and Accept the Request Talk to Usu-chu to hear the details of the next request. Place the Port Streetlight to Clear Pick up the "Port Streetlight" nearby and place it near the utility pole you just installed. There is no specific required location as long as it is near the wind turbine and in a spot where the power lines connect to the Port Streetlight. Accept a Request from Trubbish Talk to Trubbish and accept their request. Move to the top of the lighthouse with Trubbish The request will be cleared once you reach the top of the lighthouse together with Trubbish. Since there are rubble and holes along the way, use Rock Smash to clear the debris and fill the holes with blocks to ensure Trubbish can pass through. Place Utility Poles and Connect Them to the Top of the Lighthouse After clearing Trubbish's request, place utility poles and connect the electric wires to the top of the lighthouse for later story progression. You can connect them to the top by placing utility poles using the pre-installed "Gray Circular Floors" as a guide. Accept a Request from Piplup Piplup has a speech bubble, so talk to it and accept the request. Take Piplup to the Hydroelectric Power Machine Location Head to the location of the Hydroelectric Power Machine together with Piplup. Break the blocks in the back to let the water flow Break the blocks blocking the nearby pond to let the water flow to where the waterway is. Once the water flows, the hydroelectric power machine will start operating, allowing you to complete Piplup's request. Talk to Torchic and Accept the Request Talk to Torchic to accept the request. Take Torchic to the Thermal Power Machine Let's take Torchic to the location of the Thermal Power Machine. It is located just to the west of the Wind Power Machine. Obtain the Utility Pole Recipe Nearby The "Utility Pole" recipe is lying on the ground in front of the Thermal Power Machine, so be sure to pick it up. As you progress through the story, the utility poles already placed on the map will not be enough, and you will need to craft more to supplement them. Activating the Thermal Power Machine The Thermal Power Machine is activated by inserting combustible materials. Any combustible material, such as Lumber, can be used. Since even a single item provides a long power generation time, one piece of Lumber is sufficient if you are just progressing through the story. Raise Brightness to 80 Points You can increase the brightness score by completing the Pokémon requests required for "Let's Brighten the Town" and by lighting the "Port Streetlights" throughout the town. If you haven't reached 80 points after doing everything, craft and place more "Port Streetlights" and light them up. Talk to Snorlax to Check the Brightness By talking to Snorlax, you can check your current brightness score. This serves as a guide for raising the brightness, so check it whenever you're curious. Talk to Usu-chu in the cave After raising the brightness to 80 points, talk to Usu-chu in the cave to trigger a dialogue event. Talk to Usu-chu and accept their request. Sending Electricity from Each Generator to the Device Connect power lines from the thermal, wind, and hydroelectric generators to the device to supply electricity. Electricity is delivered by connecting multiple utility poles; however, if you run out of poles, you will need to craft and install more. Talk to Ushuchu Once you have sent electricity to the device from the three power generators, talk to Ushuchu. Ushuchu will use a special move to brighten up the town. Talk to Snorlax in the Cave After the event with Usu-chu, let's go check on Snorlax inside the cave. Talking to it will trigger an event. Talk to Raikou on top of the cave Climb the cliff of the cave where Snorlax is and talk to the Raikou that appeared on top of the cave. By talking to it, Raikou will be registered in your Pokedex, and your Trainer Rank will increase to Hyper. "Let's Brighten Up the Town!" Cleared After the conversation with Raikou, the event progresses and returns to the conversation with Tangrowth and the others. After the event, Snorlax is registered to the Pokedex, and the Important Request "Let's Brighten Up the Town!" will be cleared. To the Next Town After clearing "Rocky Ridges Town" and "Bleak Beach Town," you can proceed to the next town, "Sparkling Skylands Town." If you haven't cleared "Rocky Ridges Town" yet, make sure to clear it first. title: Pokopia Rocky Ridges Town Walkthrough Guide
description: Walkthrough for Rocky Ridges Town in Pokemon Pokopia. Learn Strength, rescue Chef Greedent, cook to power up moves, raise Mood to 100, and meet Volcanion.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokopia Rocky Ridges Town Walkthrough Story Walkthrough 2026-03-18 Pokopia Rocky Ridges Town Walkthrough Walkthrough for Rocky Ridges Town in Pokemon Pokopia. Learn Strength, rescue Chef Greedent, cook to power up moves, raise Mood to 100, and meet Volcanion. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Rocky Ridges Town Walkthrough Head Through the Northwest Gate Head toward the Area Gate located to the northwest of the town in Withered Wastelands (the same direction where Onix was trapped). Once your Trainer Rank reaches Super, you can pass through by holding your Pokedex up to the entrance. Follow Tangrowth Once you pass through the gate, Tangrowth will guide you, so let's follow it. Go Straight and Examine the Computer for a Dialogue Event Go straight from the spot where Tangrowth stopped and examine the broken computer. The story will not progress until Tangrowth reaches the computer, so it is fine to walk slowly. Talk to Tangrowth when a speech bubble appears Wait a bit after checking the computer, and talk to Tangrowth when the speech bubble "To move heavy things..." appears. Since you'll have some time, it's fine to clear the surrounding area or move ahead with the next part of the guide. Creating a 2x2 Habitat: "Red Grassland" Let's create a 2x2 habitat, "Red Grassland". You can create it by using "Water Gun" on nearby withered grassland or by growing grass with Leafage. Become Friends with Scorbunny and Accept a Request To find out where Machoke is, let's become friends with "Scorbunny." They will give you hints about Machoke's habitat during the conversation. Create a Machoke Habitat Near the Crafting Table Use the "Sandbags" near the crafting table to create the Machoke habitat, "Grassy Training Ground." Befriend Machoke and Receive a Request You can become friends with Machoke after investigating the tremors at the Training Ground. After the conversation, follow Machoke; once you reach the destination, you can receive a request. Pick up 5 Stones near Machoke Once the request begins, first pick up 5 "Stones" lying around the area. Move the Rock to Machoke's Location with Strength Once you finish collecting Stones, Ditto will learn the new move "Strength". Since you will now be able to move rocks, carry one to where Machoke is located. It is fine as long as the rock is in Machoke's vicinity. Return the PC to its original spot using Strength Return to where the broken PC is and use Strength to move it to the switch's location. The PC needs to be placed facing away from the Pokémon Center, so change its orientation while using Strength. Once placed correctly, the PC will be restored and ready for use. An Important Request occurs After restoring the PC, the Important Request "Fix the Pokémon Center!" will occur. Since completing it doesn't affect the main story, you can proceed with it whenever you like. Talk to Tangrowth and Follow Him Once the PC is restored, talk to Tangrowth. After the conversation, Tangrowth will start running, so follow him. Stand on the wooden crate and use Cut on the chain Once you reach your destination, use "Cut" on the chain that the barrel is hanging from. Since you cannot reach it from the ground, climb onto the wooden crate to adjust your height. Creating the "Rocks and Grass in the Shade of the Triangular Tree" Habitat After the conversation in the kitchen, create the "Rocks and Grass in the Shade of the Triangular Tree" habitat to make friends with Dartrix. Grow four red grasses around the tree in the southwest of the map and carry the rock near the tree to complete it. Befriend Dartrix and Accept the Request Once you have befriended Dartrix, talk to it again to accept its request. In exchange for making a cutting board, it will ask you to make a perch. Pick up the Perch Recipe Pick up the Perch recipe near the stairs on the way to "Rocks and grass in the shade of a triangular tree". Craft a Perch and Place it Near the Habitat Once you have obtained the Perch recipe, collect the materials and craft it. Place the crafted perch near Dartrix's habitat, "Rocks and Grass in the Triangular Tree Shade." Report to Dartrix to Complete the Request By reporting to Dartrix, the request will be completed and you will obtain the recipe for the "Cutting Board." Crafting a Cutting Board Use the recipe you've learned to craft a Cutting Board. Lumber can be processed by giving "Small Logs," which are obtained when breaking trees or obstacles, to a Pokémon that can use Cut. Please note that processing requires a certain amount of time to pass. Place a Cutting Board and Make a Salad By placing a cutting board in any location, you will be able to cook. First, let's make the salad required for the request. Eat Salad to Strengthen Leafage Eating a Plain Salad you've made will fully restore your PP and strengthen "Leafage." With the strengthened Leafage, you can grow grass in a 5-tile cross pattern by holding down ZR, and under certain conditions, you will be able to grow aquatic plants and moss. Head to Tangrowth's location for a dialogue event Head to the location where Tangrowth is, and a dialogue event will begin. Head to the cave on the west side of the map Head to the cave blocked by rocks on the west side of the map. You can proceed by using Rock Smash. Create the "Mossy Hot Spring" Habitat at the Cave's Waterside Proceed a little further into the cave and create the "Mossy Hot Spring" habitat at the water's edge. The moss required for its creation can be grown by using an enhanced Leafage move inside the cave. Become friends with Torkoal and accept their request After becoming friends with Torkoal, talk to them again to accept their request. Preparing the Path from Mossy Hot Spring to the Poke Center To complete Torkoal's request, let's prepare the path to the Poke Center. It's important to make it easier to walk by installing stairs where there are ledges, breaking walls, and growing moss on the ground. It's More Efficient to Let Torkoal Walk First When carrying out Torkoal's request, it's efficient to go ahead and prepare the path while Torkoal is walking. Since Torkoal walks slowly and will stop when it encounters an obstacle—allowing you to restart from that same spot each time—you can get by with minimal path preparation while keeping an eye on Torkoal. Deliver Torkoal to the Pokemon Center to Clear Talk to Torkoal once it has reached the Pokemon Center to clear the request and learn the Bread Oven recipe. Crafting a Bread Oven Volcanic ash, the material for the bread oven, can be obtained from gray blocks found in the field. Once you have crafted the bread oven, place it wherever you like. Break the rocks above the field to restore the river's flow Go up to the source of the river in the field in the southwest of the map and break the multiple rocks blocking the water. It's complete once the bottom-most sprinkler activates. Harvesting Wheat Once the sprinkler has been running for a while, let's harvest the wheat planted nearby. You can harvest 3 units per tile, which will allow you to make bread. Bring Scorbunny to the Bread Oven and Bake Bread Bring Scorbunny to the bread oven and bake bread together. Eat Bread to Strengthen Cut Once the bread is ready, take it out from your inventory and eat it. Cut will be strengthened, allowing you to break things like wire mesh and chains by holding ZR. Use Cut on the Chain Again to Rescue Chef Greedent When you cut the chain with the upgraded "Cut," a Greedent dressed as a chef will appear from inside the barrel. Greedent will be registered in your Pokédex during the conversation event. Talk to Chef Baris in front of the Pokemon Center After rescuing Chef Baris, talk to him in front of the Pokemon Center. Talk to Chef Barisu in the Kitchen to Receive a Request After the conversation at the Poke Center, head to the kitchen to receive a request from Chef Barisu. Since you have to wait for Chef Barisu to move, there is no need to rush. Talk to Tangrowth Return to the Pokémon Center and talk to Tangrowth. After the conversation, you will obtain the "Frying Pan" recipe. Talk to Machoke and Follow Him Talk to the Machoke standing near the tracks. After the conversation, he will start heading further in, so follow him. Break the wire fence with powered-up Cut Machoke will guide you to the wire fence, so break it with a powered-up Cut. If your powered-up PP has run out, eat some bread again to power up Cut. Create the "Dig and Burn" Habitat Go past the wire fence and use the items near the blast furnace to create the "Dig and Burn" habitat. It will be completed by combining the Blast Furnace, Wheelbarrow, and Mining Tools. Become friends with Magmar and accept their request Become friends with Magmar and talk to them again to accept their request. Put Copper into the Smelter Put Copper into the "Smelter" and craft 2 "Copper Ingots." After putting in the Copper, Copper Ingots will be produced if you are accompanied by a Pokémon skilled at "Kindling," such as Scorbunny or Magmar. Obtain Copper from nearby brown walls Copper can be obtained from the brown walls in the passage leading to the Smelter. Use Rock Smash to break the blocks where brown ore is embedded. Craft a Frying Pan and Report to Chef Baris Take the finished Copper Ingots out of the furnace and craft a Frying Pan. Harvest 4 Beans Harvest 4 beans at the field in the southwest of the map. If the river is open, you can travel to the field and harvest them immediately. Making a Plain Hamburg Once you have a Frying Pan and 4 Beans, go to where Chef Baris is located. You can cook by placing the Frying Pan on the stove, so add the 4 Beans to make a Plain Hamburg. Eat a Hamburger to Strengthen Rock Smash Once you have made a Plain Hamburger, take it out from your inventory and eat it. The move "Rock Smash" will be strengthened, allowing you to break harder ores and other objects. Listen to Machoke's Request Speak to the Machoke located near the Pokémon Center. He will ask you to find Graveler. Create a "Mossy Rock" in the Cave Head to the cave with the hot spring where Torkoal was, and let's create the habitat "Mossy Rock". Become Friends with Graveler and Learn "Rollout" After talking to Graveler and becoming friends, talk to it again to receive a request. You will learn the new move "Rollout," allowing you to move around the field while rolling. Create the "Mossy Rock" Habitat in the Cave Use "Rollout" and speak to Machoke while in the form of Graveler. Report to Graveler Return to the cave and report to Graveler to complete the request. Accept Dartrix's Request Talk to Dartrix to accept a request from them. Make Shredded Salad with Dartrix Have Dartrix accompany you and make Shredded Salad together. If Dartrix is not with you, it will become a Plain Salad, so make sure to cook while Dartrix is accompanying you. Talk to Dartrix after cooking to complete the request. Reach Environment Level 3 The next objective, "Let's Throw a Party!", cannot be started unless your Environment Level is at least 3. You can efficiently raise your Environment Level by picking up sparkles on the island to create new habitats and increasing the number of undiscovered Pokemon. How to Raise Environment Level and Unlocks Habitat Pokedex List Talk to Scorbunny Once your Environment Level reaches 3, Scorbunny will appear on the east side of the map, so go and talk to it. Talk to Agerotom past the volcanic ash Proceed forward while breaking the volcanic ash in front of Scorbunny using "Rollout." Go over the first ledge and talk to Agerotom on your left. Go outside and report to Scorbunny Go outside and report the source of the sound to Scorbunny. Talk to Rotom-A in the plaza past the stairs Wait a short while and Rotom-A will emerge from the cave and head toward the plaza. Once it arrives at the plaza and a speech bubble appears, talk to it to trigger the Important Request "Let's Have a Party!". Talk to Chef Ballis and Place the Pot Talk to Chef Ballis in the plaza to receive a Party Pot. Place it in an open spot in front of Chef Ballis, then talk to him again. Accept Agerotom's Request Talk to Agerotom in the plaza to accept their request. Give the CD to Agerotom to Clear Once you find a CD, talk to Agerotom and select "About the CD..." to give it to him. Giving one CD will clear the request. CD located in the bookshelf near Agerotom There is a "Mt. Moon" CD in the bookshelf on the right side of the stage in the plaza where Agerotom is located. If you don't have any CDs, obtain one here and give it to him. Bring Pokémon that are good at "Cheer Up" Befriend Pokémon that are good at "Cheer Up" and bring them to the plaza. Agerotom recommends Ludicolo, but any Pokémon that is good at "Cheer Up" will work, including those from other areas. Kricketot and Diglett are recommended as they are easy to find When gathering "Cheer Up" Pokémon, Kricketot and Diglett are recommended because they are easy to find. It is more efficient to simply create habitats for high-rarity Pokémon like Ludicolo and Cinderace while you aim to recruit them. Accept Tangrowth's Request Talk to Tangrowth in the Plaza and accept its request. You will be asked to bring a "Large Lost Item." Hand over the Large Lost Item to clear Hand over the Large Lost Item in your possession to Tangrowth to clear the request. After clearing it, you can have Large Lost Items appraised by talking to Tangrowth. Large Lost Items are inside glowing volcanic ash You can obtain a Large Lost Item by breaking the glowing volcanic ash on the plaza stage. It is also recommended to break any other glowing blocks you find in the field. Displaying the Appraised Big Lost Item Let's display the Big Lost Item you had appraised in the Plaza. There is no specific location required as long as it is within the Plaza. After placing it, report to Professor Tangrowth to complete the request. Accept Chef Baris's Request Talk to Chef Baris to accept his request. After the conversation, you will obtain the recipe for the Party Plate. Craft 5 Party Plates Craft 5 Party Plates as requested by Chef Ballis. You will need a total of 5 "Iron Ingots," so smelt Iron in the "Blast Furnace" to make "Iron Ingots." Iron is in the cave where Agerotom was Iron can be mined from the walls of the cave where Agerotom was. Look for ore embedded in gray blocks, and use Rock Smash to break those sections. Cook 5 dishes of your choice Let's cook 5 dishes to put on the party plate. There are no specific requirements for the dishes, so Salad is recommended as it requires fewer materials. Grow grass with Leafage and use Cut to harvest "Leaves," the material for Salad, can be efficiently collected by growing grass with Leafage and then using Cut. You can keep obtaining them until your PP runs out, so repeat this until you have collected 10 Leaves. Place Party Plates Around the Pot Place 5 Party Plates around the pot in the plaza where Rotom is located. There is no specific arrangement required; once you have placed the plates, don't forget to put the dishes you prepared into each one. Report to Chef Baris to Complete the Request Once you have placed the Party Plate, report to Chef Baris to complete the request. Raise Mood to 100 Points Once you have cleared all the requests, let's raise the Mood to 100 points. Mood can be increased efficiently by bringing along many Pokémon that are good at "Boosting." If you get stuck while raising the Mood, it is also recommended to purchase decorations from the Shop and place them in large quantities. Talk to Rotom-Hype to check the Mood By talking to Rotom-Hype and selecting "What's the current Mood?", you can check your current Mood score. It serves as a benchmark for raising the Mood, so be sure to check it whenever you need to. Speak to Chef Greedent After raising the Mood to 100 points, speak to Chef Greedent. You will be asked to collect ingredients for the curry. Collect the Ingredients Needed for Curry Collect four types of ingredients needed for curry. Wheat and beans can be harvested from the fields on Mt. Rugged, and Honey can be gathered from sparkling spots on flowers or obtained through Combee's specialty. Making Curry with 5 Pokemon Make curry with five Pokemon, including Chef Baris. If there aren't four in the plaza, you will need to bring them from their habitats. Talk to Volcanion at the Volcano After making curry, an event will begin and Volcanion will appear at the summit of the volcano. Climb the outer wall of the volcano to reach the summit and talk to Volcanion. Complete the Important Request after talking to Tangrowth After descending the mountain and talking to Tangrowth, the Important Request will be completed. As a clear reward, you will obtain recipes for the "Launching Tube" and "Firework Ball." To the next town Once you have cleared "Rocky Ridges Town," head to "Bleak Beach Town." If you have cleared both "Rocky Ridges Town" and "Bleak Beach Town," your next destination will be "Sparkling Skylands Town." title: Pokopia Withered Wastelands Town Story Walkthrough Guide
description: Step-by-step walkthrough for Withered Wastelands Town in Pokemon Pokopia. Learn Water Gun, befriend Bulbasaur and Charmander, raise Hydration to 75, and meet Kyogre.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokopia Withered Wastelands Town Story Walkthrough Story Walkthrough 2026-03-17 Pokopia Withered Wastelands Town Story Walkthrough Step-by-step walkthrough for Withered Wastelands Town in Pokemon Pokopia. Learn Water Gun, befriend Bulbasaur and Charmander, raise Hydration to 75, and meet Kyogre. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Withered Wastelands Town Walkthrough Player Character Appearance Settings When you start the game, you'll first decide your protagonist's appearance. Your avatar's appearance can be changed even after progressing through the story, so if you're unsure, it's perfectly fine to set it once and proceed. Talk to the Tangrowth in Front of You Once you gain control, try talking to the Tangrowth right in front of you. Collect "Stone" and "Lumber" Near the Tangrowth In the area where you talk to Tangrowth, "Stone" and "Lumber" are scattered. While you're talking to him, pick them up with the Y button or suck them up to collect them. Investigate the Glowing Spot in Front of Tangrowth Investigate the glowing cart in front of Tangrowth. You can obtain the Pokédex from it. Deciding Your Player Name Once set, your name cannot be changed even after the story progresses, so please carefully check your input before confirming. Following Tangrowth After entering your player name and completing the basic settings, follow Tangrowth. When a yellow speech bubble appears above Tangrowth's head, talk to it to proceed. Head to Squirtle Follow Tangrowth, proceed through the passage, and talk to Squirtle. Pokémon with Problems Display Speech Bubbles If a speech bubble appears above a Pokémon's head on the field, it's a sign that the Pokémon is either in some kind of trouble or has something it wants to convey. To understand the situation, try talking to them. Hit Squirtle with "Water Gun" By talking to Squirtle, you can learn the "Water Gun" move. Since learned moves can be activated with the ZR button, hit Squirtle with "Water Gun" and rescue it. Revive a 2x2 Grassland with Water Gun Use Water Gun on the 2x2 withered grassland in front of you to revive the "Green Grassland" habitat. This Water Gun can restore withered land and trees to their original state by using it on them. Check the Shaking Grass and Talk to Bulbasaur Once habitat restoration is complete and a certain amount of time has passed, the grass may start to shake. When you investigate that shaking grass, Bulbasaur will appear and join your team. By talking to Bulbasaur, you will be able to accept requests from him. Hit 10 Withered Grass with Water Gun To fulfill Bulbasaur's request, let's revive 10 withered grass scattered around with Water Gun. If you become unsure of your current progress or objective, open the menu with the + button and check the request details. Report to Bulbasaur and Complete the Request Once you've hit 10 withered grass patches with "Water Gun," talk to Bulbasaur and report. As a reward, you can learn the move "Razor Leaf," which allows you to grow grass on the ground. Talk to Squirtle and Accept a Request A speech bubble icon is displayed above Squirtle's head, so talk to it and accept the request. Create Another New Green Grassland Utilize 'Leaf' to establish another "Green Grassland" habitat nearby. There's no need to stick to a 2x2 shape; it's fine to place it adjacent to an existing grassland. Clear the Request by Talking to Squirtle The request will be cleared by talking to the nearby Squirtle. Talk to Tangrowth Once you complete Squirtle's request, speak to Tangrowth. They will then instruct you to collect the Pinap Berries scattered around and distribute them to Squirtle and Bulbasaur. Headbutt Nearby Trees to Get Leppa Berries Press the A button towards a nearby tree to perform Headbutt and obtain a Leppa Berry. If you can't find any trees nearby, use Water Gun to regenerate a tree, then perform Headbutt. Consume Food to Restore PP Consuming food items dropped on the field, such as Leppa Berries and Carrots, will restore the PP displayed in the bottom right of the screen. If PP runs out, you won't be able to use moves, so it's important to regularly replenish your food supply during your adventure. Give Leppa Berries to Squirtle and Bulbasaur Once you obtain Leppa Berries from the tree, give them to the Squirtle and Bulbasaur walking nearby. After Reporting to Tangrowth, Place a Chair and Sit When you talk to Tangrowth, you will obtain a "Log Chair." Open your inventory with the X button, select the "Log Chair" you obtained, then place it with the A button and sit down. Talk to Bulbasaur to Unlock the Crafting Table As soon as your conversation with Tangrowth ends, follow Bulbasaur and talk to it. During this interaction, you will obtain "Simple Wooden Recipes". Craft a Bonfire and Place it Next to Tangrowth Craft the bonfire requested by Bulbasaur and place it next to Tangrowth. To craft the bonfire, you will need one "Sturdy Branch" and one "Stone", both of which can be found lying on the ground nearby. Create a Green Grassland and Befriend Charmander Create a 2x2 Green Grassland nearby and befriend Charmander. After creating the Grassland, please wait for a while. Then, you can find Charmander by examining the shaking grass. Lead Charmander to the Bonfire After befriending Charmander, talk to him and lead him to the bonfire's location to trigger a specific event. At this point, by choosing the "Let's go together" option, Charmander will begin to follow the player. Talk to Tangrowth to Activate the PC After completing the bonfire event, go around the map and talk to Tangrowth, who is in front of the broken Pokémon Center. Operate the PC, and once you complete the displayed tutorial, the PC will become usable. Complete the Three Challenges Displayed on the PC After finishing your conversation with Tangrowth, clear the three challenges that can be checked from the PC. PC Functions: Shop and Item Reception The PC installed in front of the Pokémon Center allows you to check "Challenges," shop at the "Shop," and "Receive Items." By using the Shop function, you can spend coins to purchase furniture, recipes, seeds, and more. These items will likely be effectively utilized later in features such as the housing function, which will be unlocked. Create the "Shady Grassland" and Befriend Timburr By placing 4 Grass near the rocks, the habitat "Shady Grassland" will be completed. After a short while, you can encounter Timburr and complete "Search for Pokémon! ①". Investigate Sparkles to Obtain Habitat Hints By interacting with the Sparkles present in the field, clues about Pokémon habitats will be registered in your Pokédex. To befriend Pokémon, it is recommended to actively investigate Sparkles. Collecting Sturdy Branches and Watering Withered Trees Find and pick up "Sturdy Branches" near the withered trees scattered across the field, and water those trees. To complete this challenge, you need to collect 5 withered trees and 10 "Sturdy Branches." Befriend Scyther and Complete the Request It's recommended to deepen your friendship with Scyther and complete the request, as you'll be able to learn "Cut," a move you'll use frequently as you progress through the story. If you hand over 2 "Sturdy Branches" to Scyther, you will be able to use Cut. How to Learn and Use Cut Scyther's Habitat and Specialties Clear Grass and Wood Debris with Cut Grass and wood debris found on the field can be destroyed using Cut. If used on grass, you have a certain chance to obtain "Leaf." If you destroy wood debris, you can obtain "Small Log" and also clear a path. After Completing the Challenge Report, Talk to Bulbasaur Once you've finished reporting the challenge on the computer, talk to Bulbasaur to accept a new request. Make a "Hay Bed" at the Crafting Table Through conversation with Bulbasaur, you will unlock the recipe for the "Hay Bed." Afterwards, begin crafting it at the Crafting Table. The necessary "Leaves" can be obtained probabilistically by breaking grass using Cut. Achieve the Objective by Placing a Bed Near Bulbasaur By creating a Hay Bed and placing it near Bulbasaur, you can clear the request. Other Pokémon will also experience improved "Comfort" and an increased Environment Level by having their favorite items placed around them. For this reason, we recommend actively engaging in this. After Checking the PC, Talk to Tangrowth Once you complete Bulbasaur's request, check the PC, then talk to Tangrowth. To build the "Leafy Room," you need to purchase the "Leafy Room Kit" at the shop. Purchase the "Leaf Room Kit" at the Shop and Start Construction Once you obtain the "Leaf Room Kit" at the shop, place it in your preferred location. To proceed with construction, you need to gather the necessary materials and bring a Pokémon that meets the conditions to the kit's location. Place 3 pieces of furniture and report to Timburr Once you have placed 3 pieces of furniture inside the Leafy Room, go report to Timburr. Furniture can be purchased at the shop, allowing you to place it in your room at home. Take Charmander to Tangrowth By talking to Charmander and guiding them to Tangrowth's location, you can obtain the Ditto flag during this event. Place Ditto's Flag Outside the Leaf Room Place Ditto's Flag outside the Leaf Room. By placing this flag, that location will function as your home, allowing you to freely arrange furniture and live with your favorite Pokémon. Furthermore, by using "Home Navigator" found in the + Menu, you can return home anytime. Construct the "Gym Break Room" Habitat To recruit a Hitmonchan that knows "Rock Smash," let's set up the "Gym Break Room" Habitat. The Sandbag is immediately west of the broken Pokémon Center The Sandbag, essential for creating the "Gym Break Room" Rest Area, is located immediately west of the broken Pokémon Center. Once you obtain the Sandbag, place it next to the bench, which is beside the sparkle northwest of the Pokémon Center. Befriend Hitmonchan and Complete the Request Once you've become friends with Hitmonchan, talk to them again and accept the request. This request can be completed by handing over 2 Stones. Learning "Rock Smash" Upon completing Hitmonchan's request, you will learn "Rock Smash". By using this move, you will be able to destroy blocks present on the map, allowing you to secure paths or advance into unexplored areas. Talk to Squirtle and Accept a Request Speak to Squirtle, who is located to the west of the damaged Pokémon Center, and accept the request. Destroy the Wall with Rock Smash and Proceed to the Cave Destroy the wall in front of you with Rock Smash and proceed to the cave on your right. Dig Your Way Towards the Source of the Voice and Talk to Onix As you proceed in the direction of the mysterious voice heard deep within the cave, numerous blocks destructible with 'Rock Smash' obstruct your path. Dig through these blocks to advance, and talk to Onix. Talk to Tangrowth and Break the Southern Wall When you talk to Tangrowth to ask how to rescue Onix, you will first be asked to break the southern wall. Use 'Rock Smash' to destroy the southern wall and open a path beyond it. Investigate the Entrance to the Left Tower After completing the series of events on the sandy beach, investigate the entrance to the tower visible on your left. This investigation will trigger the important request "Take on the Entrance Challenge," but it does not affect the main story progression of Withered Wastelands town, so it's fine to postpone it. You will revisit this location in the final stages of the story, so it's reassuring to know its location now. Entrance Challenge Strategy List of Important Requests Deepen Your Friendship with Magikarp and Complete the Quest It's recommended to talk to the Magikarp floating on the water's surface, become friends with it, and complete its quest. The quest can be completed by placing a fishing rod next to a log chair, and as a clear reward, "Splash (Jump)" will become available. Talk to Tangrowth in front of the Pokémon Center After finishing the event at the "Entry Challenge Tower", speak to the Tangrowth in front of the Pokémon Center. Immediately after the event ends, Tangrowth will be moving slowly, so you will need to wait until it arrives at the Pokémon Center. Become Friends with Slowpoke and Accept the Request Since you need to take Slowpoke to Tangrowth, first become friends with Slowpoke and accept the related request. Slowpoke appears in an area called "Seashore Grassland." Prepare the Path to the Pokémon Center and Guide Slowpoke Once you become friends with Slowpoke, prepare the path leading to the Pokémon Center to fulfill his request. In areas with elevation differences, install "Wooden Stairs", and on flat ground, by wetting it with "Water Gun", Slowpoke can proceed without hindrance. Tips for Letting Slowpoke Lead and Efficiently Preparing the Path When fulfilling Slowpoke's request, if the player goes ahead and prepares the path while Slowpoke is walking, the work can be advanced efficiently. Slowpoke's walking speed is slow, and even if it gets stuck, it will stop in place, allowing you to retry from the same position as many times as needed. Therefore, by keeping a close eye on Slowpoke, you can proceed without issue with minimal path preparation. Talk to Tangrowth After delivering Slowpoke to the Pokémon Center and a series of events progresses, a new objective will begin: "Let's make it rain with Yawn!" To succeed in this Yawn-induced rainfall, it is essential to prepare the surroundings into a sufficiently moist environment. Destroy the Northwest Wall of the Broken Pokémon Center to Form a Pond Destroy the wall located northwest of the Broken Pokémon Center using Rock Smash to generate a water flow. Once water flows and a pond is formed, you can also destroy the surrounding rocks to widen the waterway, which will expand the pond's size and increase the Moisture Level. Destroy the Northeast Wall of the Broken Pokémon Center and Create a Pond Also, create a pond beyond the wall located northeast of the broken Pokémon Center, which you remove with "Rock Smash". The water source is located a little way up that wall, and by installing a "Horsea Fountain" after the pond is completed, you can expect even higher scores. Learn "Cultivate" by Completing Drilbur's Request Drilbur's request, which appears when you destroy the wall and proceed, can also be completed by creating a pond. As a reward, the action "Cultivate," which allows you to cultivate the ground and plant seeds, will be unlocked. Break the Wall to the Right of the Crafting Table to Create a Pond A water source is similarly hidden to the right of the Crafting Table. Therefore, use "Rock Smash" to destroy the wall and create a pond. You can only obtain a total of 2 Horsea Fountains, combining those placed on the map and those available for purchase in the shop. Therefore, you cannot install a Horsea Fountain in ponds created from the third one onwards. There's Also a Water Source in Front of the Admission Challenge Tower A water source is also buried behind the wall, immediately in front of the Admission Challenge Tower. Don't forget to destroy this one too and form a pond. Talk to Slowpoke After the two ponds are complete, talk to Slowpoke. While no special conversation event will occur, this interaction with Slowpoke is a prerequisite for accepting subsequent requests. Talk to Squirtle and Accept the Request To increase the "Moisture" value, talk to Squirtle and accept the request. Place 4 Grass around the Waterfront By placing 4 Grass around the waterfront, you will complete the "Lush Grassland" habitat, which is required to fulfill Squirtle's request. Talk to Squirtle to Complete the Request By talking to Squirtle again, the request from him will be completed. Take Squirtle to the Lush Grassland After completing Squirtle's request, talk to it again, and it will express a desire to move to the Lush Grassland. Select "Let's go together" and guide it to the destination. When you select "Move here?" at the location, Squirtle's residence relocation will be complete. Explore the Map and Raise Hydration to 75 Points Once you have completed creating the pond and Squirtle's request, simply explore the map and raise the Hydration level. For all withered trees found in the field, continue to use "Water Gun" until the Hydration level reaches 75 points. Have Slowpoke Use "Yawn" to Check the Score While raising the Hydration level, you can check the current score by having Slowpoke use "Yawn". As it serves as a guide for your progress, it's a good idea to check it regularly if you want to keep track of your situation. Furthermore, when the Hydration level reaches 75 points, a speech bubble will appear above Squirtle's head. Reach 75 Moisture Points! Talk to Squirtle Once your Moisture reaches 75 points, speak to Squirtle and accept his request. Upon accepting the request, the habitat "Rain Dance Spot" will be unlocked, and you will be asked to help prepare for the Rain Dance. Obtain Castform Dolls in the First Cave There are two Castform Dolls, necessary for creating a Rain Dance Spot, located inside the cave you visit right after starting the game. After heading south and entering the cave, try examining the cart where the Pokédex was stored. Video: Accessing the First Cave Set Up the Rain Prayer Spot and Guide Squirtle Let's guide Squirtle to its habitat, the "Rain Prayer Spot." After Squirtle finishes eating the berries, you will be instructed to confirm that Slowpoke yawns. After the Slowpoke Yawn Event, Head to the Seaside When you go to witness Slowpoke's yawn, it will perform a magnificent, perfect 100-point yawn, causing it to rain. Once this event is complete, proceed to the southern seaside where a loud cry was heard. Open the Path to Kyogre and Talk to It After completing the event at the beach, build a bridge to Kyogre's location and talk to it. To build this bridge, you first need to obtain the "Pier Plank Recipe" which has fallen behind the crafting table, and then craft "Pier Planks." As you progress through the conversation with Kyogre, it will join your team, and your Trainer Rank will simultaneously be promoted to Super. After the Kyogre Event, Head to Onix's Location Once the series of events with Kyogre is complete, move to Onix's location. By destroying the wall in front of Onix with 'Rock Smash', the 'Stomping Tantrum' move will be unlocked and become usable. Onix's Main Appearance Locations and Characteristics 'Stomping Tantrum''s Capabilities and a List of Pokémon That Can Utilize This Move Talk to Tangrowth to Complete the Important Request After helping Onix, talk to Tangrowth to complete the Important Request "Make it Rain with Yawn!". Once you clear this request, you will be able to proceed from Withered Wastelands Town to the next areas: "Rocky Ridges Town" or "Bleak Beach Town". title: Pokemon Pokopia Underwater Farming: How to Grow Crops with Bubbles Guide
description: Learn how underwater farming works in Pokemon Pokopia. Use Cultivate to make a field, plant seeds, then use a Water-specialty Pokemon or Bubble Machine to grow crops in Bubbly Basin.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokemon Pokopia Underwater Farming: How to Grow Crops with Bubbles Gameplay Guides 2026-08-07 Pokemon Pokopia Underwater Farming: How to Grow Crops with Bubbles Learn how underwater farming works in Pokemon Pokopia. Use Cultivate to make a field, plant seeds, then use a Water-specialty Pokemon or Bubble Machine to grow crops in Bubbly Basin. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Underwater farming lets you grow crops on the Bubbly Basin seafloor instead of relying only on land fields. The loop is simple, but the condition is different from ordinary farming: after making a field and planting seeds, the crop needs bubbles . A Pokemon with the Water specialty can provide them, and a powered Bubble Machine is the convenient alternative for a permanent underwater plot. Underwater Farming Requirements Requirement Why it matters Access to Bubbly Basin Underwater fields are made on the seafloor. Cultivate Turns usable ground into a field for seeds. Seeds The crop must be planted after the field is made. Water-specialty Pokemon or Bubble Machine Supplies the bubbles needed for underwater growth. Cultivate is the Ditto action used to make a field. If it is not available yet, finish Drilbur's request first. For a crop that is especially useful in the DLC, see Watermelon and Cut Watermelon : Watermelon can be processed into the Smoothie ingredient needed for faster underwater travel. How to Grow Crops Underwater Dive to a clear section of the seafloor in Bubbly Basin. Use Cultivate on the ground to make a field. Plant the seeds you want to grow. Ask a nearby Pokemon with the Water specialty to apply bubbles to the planted field. Wait for the crop to mature, then harvest it normally. The important part is step four. Planting seeds alone does not finish the underwater farming loop. The bubbles are the care action that lets the planted crop grow. Place the helper close to the field so the plot is easy to maintain rather than scattering seeds across a large part of the seabed. Use a Bubble Machine for a Permanent Plot The Bubble Machine is a DLC utility item that emits bubbles when it receives power. Put it next to muddy ground or underwater crops to make a small farm easier to manage. It is a good choice for a plot you expect to revisit, such as a Watermelon field beside the Bubbly Basin town. The machine still needs electricity. Plan its position before filling the area with crops and decoration, then connect it to a suitable power source. This avoids having to rebuild the field just to run power into the middle of it. The Bubble Machine is found in Bubbly Basin and can also appear on an underwater Dream Island. Water-specialty Pokemon or Bubble Machine? Situation Better option A small temporary field A Water-specialty Pokemon A farm beside your usual route Bubble Machine You have not set up power yet A Water-specialty Pokemon You are building a larger decorated farm Bubble Machine A Water-specialty Pokemon is the lower-setup option. It works well while testing a crop or while you are still progressing through the DLC. A Bubble Machine is more practical for repeatable farming because it keeps the bubble source at the field instead of depending on where a helper happens to be placed. Practical Layout Tips Keep the farm compact at first. Make a field, plant one crop type, and place the bubble source along the edge where it will remain reachable. Leave a clear route for harvesting and for moving around while diving. Once the growing loop works, expand the field in sections instead of placing a large number of seeds before confirming that all of them can receive bubbles. Watermelon is a useful first crop because it connects directly to the Smoothie chain. Grow Watermelon, have a Pokemon with the Cut Trees specialty process it into Cut Watermelon, then use it in the Mixer. The resulting Smoothies enable Surf while Diving, so a nearby underwater farm can shorten preparation for long cave routes. Common Problems The seeds are planted but the crop is not growing Check that the field is receiving bubbles. Move a Water-specialty Pokemon closer, or use a powered Bubble Machine beside the crop. The planted field needs that underwater care step after the seeds go in. I cannot make a field on the seafloor Use Cultivate on suitable ground, not on an occupied tile. If you have not unlocked Cultivate, complete Drilbur's request before returning to the underwater area. Should I build a huge underwater farm immediately? No. Start with a small plot and a reachable bubble source. A permanent powered machine is worth adding once you know the crop route you want to repeat. title: Pokopia Patch Notes & Version History Guide
description: Read the full Pokopia Ver. 2.0.0 patch notes from August 5, 2026, plus bug fixes and update history. See the latest changes and older versions.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokopia Patch Notes & Version History About Pokopia 2026-08-09 Pokopia Patch Notes & Version History Read the full Pokopia Ver. 2.0.0 patch notes from August 5, 2026, plus bug fixes and update history. See the latest changes and older versions. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Get patch notes on Discord Receive full patch notes and update alerts as soon as a new version is posted. Join our Discord Update History This page tracks the latest Pokopia update details. New versions will be added here as soon as they are available. Ver. 2.0.0 (August 5, 2026) Additions Added all content for the Expansion Pass - Bubbly Basin Added the move Dive, allowing players to move freely underwater. The Build specialty can now be used to build houses underwater. Added new items such as the portal pod and safe. Added the new pattern, dynamic Ditto print. Added new emotes: Lie Down and Ready, Set, Go! Added five new hair colors: orange, light pink, yellow-green, blue-green, and brown. Added a function to move items in bulk between the storage box and bag. Added a function to delete items placed inside objects such as the garbage bin. Added the ability to fine-tune depth placement when placing windows, doors, and similar items. Added an option in Settings to hide the confirmation message shown when canceling Magnet Rise. Added an option in Settings allowing movement while the move wheel is open. Added motion-sickness reduction settings for the camera. The following items can now be painted: stylish stool, handrail, metal chain, workbench, vending machine, bike, bookcase, Pokémon Center counter, arrow sign, rope. Improvements Even if a Pokémon's habitat is destroyed, it will move back in if the same habitat is rebuilt within a certain area. Pokémon that are sad because furniture was removed will now notice more quickly when the same furniture is replaced. Pokémon that taught you an emote will now respond with the same emote when you use it. If a Pokémon being searched for in the Pokédex is in another town, you can now travel to that town using Return Home. Reduced ordinary conversation indicators so that special Pokémon conversations and requests directed at Ditto stand out more clearly. Lost relics can now be appraised in batches of up to 10 at a time. Paint, Gather Honey, and Collect can now be performed multiple times in the same interaction. During crafting, materials in the storage box next to the workbench will be consumed before materials in the bag. Increased the placement limit for power generators (excluding furnaces) from 64 to 128. Increased the number of different photos that can be displayed in a town from 10 to 40. When sucking up liquid, a short press of the move button to hold liquids in Ditto's mouth will allow liquid to be held in their mouth without removing it from the environment. When releasing stored water, adjusted water levels now automatically match nearby water levels. Smearguru can now learn patterns from photos stored in References. Improved visibility of the target item when painting with paint balloons. Increased the amount of treasure discoverable with the Dowsing Machine on Dream Islands. Pokémon companions can now follow you while moving with Surf, Glide, Rollout, or Magnet Rise. Inhaling items and opening the bag are now possible while rolling using Rollout. Rollout can now destroy certain natural objects such as large boulders. Surf can now be activated on land by pressing the Surf button while holding the focus button. Improved activation conditions for Surf and Waterfall so they occur more smoothly. Leafage can now be used on farm soil to revert it to a normal soil block. Strength can now be used underwater. Added an All tab to both the Pokédex and Habitat Dex. Made it clearer that buildings can still be remodeled even when items such as the Ditto Flag are attached to roofs or walls. During construction, any Pokémon not assigned to the Build role in a building project can now help with cooking. Prevented treasures in Sparkling Skylands from appearing when using the Dowsing Machine in locations where breaking terrain would cause them to fall. Improved messaging when there are insufficient materials for copying items using the 3D Printer. Items can now be placed on top of square plants. Hide-and-sneak can now be canceled midway. Adjusted in-game event notifications shown at startup so they are displayed only during specific remaining-day periods. Certain roof items now block water. Increased output when crafting curved eaves to 10. Tidal Bell and Clear Bell can now be triggered using laser sensors and switches. Adjusted sound effects for camping chair and sleeping bag. Improved performance for certain rendering processes. Fixes When talking to a Pokémon that is currently assigned to construct buildings, options such as "Follow me!" may sometimes fail to appear. Suicune and Gholdengo may be unable to travel across water. Pokémon may occasionally fall into the ocean or off cliffs when appearing from their habitats.
